business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid mixed legal system: Quebec private and commercial law follows the Civil Law tradition (Civil Code of Quebec); federal public, criminal and regulatory law follows the Common Law tradition; the Limited Partnership is governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (arts. 2236-2251) and the provincial Limited Partnership Act (CQLR c S-32.1).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force for Canada
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014)
Applicability must be mapped to the UBO's country of residence; Canada maintains more than 45 tax treaties and 15+ investment treaties that may individually apply.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations, administered by FINTRAC; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2 (money laundering); Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act, SC 1998, c 34; sanctions under the United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, and the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, administered by Global Affairs Canada. Provincial: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Limited Partnership Act, CQLR c S-32.1; Civil Code of Quebec, Book 4, Title 2 (Limited Partnerships). No dedicated provincial UBO register applies to Quebec LPs; beneficial owner transparency is enforced through FINTRAC-regulated institutions at onboarding and through the reporting duty of the general partner.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or official registry extract (attestation d'immatriculation) of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ); or competent corporate registry of the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Where issued by a foreign registry: Hague Apostille by the issuing state's competent authority (Canada acceded with effect from 11 January 2024); where the issuing state is not a Hague member: consular legalization at the nearest Canadian diplomatic mission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the general partner (certificat de conformite)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) or equivalent home-jurisdiction registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Global Affairs Canada for federal documents; provincial designated authority for provincial documents) or consular legalization for non-Hague states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized evidence of identity and residential address for each UBO (valid passport, government-issued photo ID, and sworn declaration of address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the issuing state's central authority; if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention party, consular legalization by the Canadian embassy or consulate having consular jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation (traduction certifiee) of every due diligence exhibit not drafted in French
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator who is a member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certification by the OTTIAQ translator; notarization of the translator's signature is recommended for foreign filing; no apostille required for intra-Quebec use.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) appointing the Quebec resident formation agent or attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in Quebec or notary public in the principal's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed in Quebec: notarial deed (acte notarie), no apostille required; if executed abroad: apostille or consular legalization per the executing state's status under the Hague Convention.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the general partner, all UBOs, and authorized signatories against the consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list (Global Affairs Canada), UN Security Council sanctions, and, because the target payment rails (Stripe, Paddle) involve US-dollar clearing, the OFAC SDN list; PEP status must be assessed using FINTRAC's guidance on politically exposed persons and domestic PEPs, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management sign-off where any PEP trigger appears; the payments processors will independently conduct KYC/AML review under the PCMLTFA as money service businesses/PSPs and will require a complete UBO breakdown, so the LP must maintain a private contractual register of limited partners' beneficial ownership at the head office.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises online portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); the name clearance procedure is the 'Recherche et reservation de nom' service.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French-language mandatory under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11: the LP's name must be declared in French; a non-French name is admitted only where it is a recognized trademark, a personal or family name, or the complement of a French name; non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) must be rendered in Latin-script phonetic transliteration and the official transliteration retained in REQ filings; French accented characters must be reproduced exactly; the LP designation may include the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' (societe en commandite).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The REQ name reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed for one additional 90-day period on payment of the regulatory fee before expiry, subject to continuing availability of the name; upon final REQ refusal, the applicant must file a written demand for reconsideration with the REQ within 30 days of the refusal, invoking statutory grounds under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (e.g., distinctiveness, compliance with the French-language rule, absence of prohibited tokens); if the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days of the reconsideration decision; counsel review is recommended before filing due to strict documentary and translation requirements.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for REQ registration purposes only if a physical street address in Quebec is designated as the LP's establishment (post-office-box-only addresses are inadmissible); a commercial virtual office suite with reception and mail handling is accepted by REQ; however, FINTRAC-regulated payment processors and the general partner's duty to maintain accounting records and the limited partners' register at an accessible Quebec address make a physical or counsel-supervised address advisable; the general partner bears unlimited liability and must maintain substantive records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 15% probability of an unannounced address-verification or records inspection within the first 36 months; REQ conducts administrative verifications of declared establishments, but FINTRAC on-site examinations are not expected for the LP itself because the LP is not a reporting entity under the PCMLTFA; the higher AML examination risk sits with Stripe and Paddle as regulated payment processors.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting fees exigible under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 2): CAD 38.75, converted at 1 USD = 1.37 CAD; subject to annual indexation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: REQ registration of the declaration of formation of the limited partnership (declaration d'immatriculation d'une societe en commandite)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff estimated at CAD 60 for a registered partnership; regulatory fee may be indexed; excludes publication fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: OTTIAQ-certified French translation package for constitutive documents and due diligence exhibits
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a 5-10 page formation package (approximately CAD 340); tariffs vary by word count, complexity and urgency.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of the UBO identification bundle and general partner incumbency documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the jurisdiction of origin; Global Affairs Canada or provincial apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rates: notarial acts CAD 80-150 per document; apostille CAD 25-50 per document; courier and legalization service CAD 50-100 per batch.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec formation agent and registered office address (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate services provider or law firm in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CAD 250-550 per year for registered office, mail forwarding, and service-of-process acceptance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, UBO/KYC analysis and PEP/sanctions screening opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec law firm (attorney licensed by the Barreau du Quebec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk ISIC 6201 software entity with two UBOs; fixed-fee CDD package includes source-of-funds review, sanctions screening and a legal opinion on the LP pass-through and liability structure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2266 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 1, 14-23, 31-40; the Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1) does not apply to a limited partnership. Filing fees are governed by the Regulation respecting the tariff of fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Quebec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of a société en commandite
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Quebec limited partnership; the partnership agreement exclusively determines capital contributions, which may be in cash, in services, or in property. No escrow account or government deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [LP NAME]: 1. THAT the Limited Partnership Agreement governing [LP NAME] is approved and adopted as submitted. 2. THAT the capital contribution of each limited partner, as set out in Schedule A, is accepted and credited; no minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by law. 3. THAT the registered office of the Partnership is situate at [address], Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is hereby notified. 4. THAT [name] is appointed as initial manager and authorized representative to execute all filings, open banking accounts and obtain all necessary permits. 5. THAT the General Partner is authorized to take all ancillary steps to give effect to the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Name Search and Distinctiveness Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online name research portal (registraire.entreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a distinctiveness search for the proposed limited partnership name against the Quebec Enterprise Register. Verify that the name includes the required legal designator ("Société en commandite", "S.E.C.", "Limited Partnership", or "L.P."). Obtain the official attestation de recherche de nom, which is valid for 90 days from issue and must accompany the registration declaration.
required_dossiers: Attestation de recherche de nom (name research certificate)
Mandate and identity documents of the general partner
Proposed partnership name and Quebec head office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for lack of distinctiveness or risk of confusion, file a revised name research request or amend the proposed name; a refusal may be challenged before the competent court under the Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel / optional notary; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the Convention de société en commandite setting out the partnership name, Quebec head office, business object (no-code web application builder and visual template services), capital contributions, profit and loss sharing, general partner's exclusive management authority, limited partners' non-administration clause, and dissolution events. Notarization is required only if the partnership receives a contribution of real property.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution records and proof of payment
Passport or government-issued ID of all partners for anti-money-laundering compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: N/A - the partnership is consensual; any defective clause is cured by executing an amending agreement before submission of the declaration of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online transactional filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic declaration selecting "Société en commandite" as the juridical form. Enter the registered name, Quebec head office address, business objects, general partner identification, and formation date. Attach the name research attestation and pay the statutory fee online. Upon approval the Registraire issues the nine-digit NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) and the limited partnership is deemed registered as of the effective date stated in the declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer queries or rejects the declaration, correct and resubmit the declaration electronically; unresolved refusals may be contested before the competent court in accordance with the legal publicity regime.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Status and Legal Publicity Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, access the public extract of the Quebec Enterprise Register and download the attestation d'immatriculation (certificate of status). Verify that the NEQ, juridical form, general and limited partner information, and head office address exactly match the executed partnership agreement. The LP's ongoing legal publicity obligations commence on the registration date.
required_dossiers: Extrait de registre (downloaded certificate of status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Material inaccuracies in the extract are rectified by filing a déclaration modificative (amendment declaration) online; failure to maintain accurate register information may attract monetary penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Activation, Banking Setup and Ancillary Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec / Canada Revenue Agency; commercial bank; local municipality and fire safety authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NEQ and attestation to open a business bank account in the limited partnership's name and to activate GST/QST and income-tax files through Revenu Québec's business portal. Since the activity is pure no-code software publishing, no professional or industrial operating permit is required; however, if a commercial office or co-working space is leased, confirm municipal occupancy compliance and landlord fire-safety certificates before employees take possession.
required_dossiers: Identity and date-of-birth records of authorized signatories
Proof of Quebec head office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec or the CRA delays tax number activation, escalate in writing through the respective business portals; CRA delays are remedied by downloading the official business number confirmation letter once enrolment completes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no Quebec industrial or professional licence is mandated for a visual web template and low-code web application builder under ISIC 6201; general enterprise registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is the only mandatory authorization. Consumer protection and Quebec Law 25 privacy obligations are administered by the Office de la protection du consommateur and the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec respectively.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - this digital service business has no manufacturing permit, environmental permit, professional licence, or financial-services licence obligation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure software/SaaS operation with no physical works or discharge activity; no EIA registration or full EIA report is required under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC emissions, or industrial solid waste generation exists. Residual IT hardware must be handled through approved end-of-life electronics recovery channels under the Règlement sur la récupération et la valorisation de produits par les entreprises (REIMR). Indirect data-centre energy emissions are outside the LP's statutory permitting scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to the digital business itself. If a commercial office or co-working space is occupied, the LP must obtain municipal occupancy and fire safety conformity attestations from the competent fire safety authority, ensure electrical and structural load compliance for any leasehold improvements, and, where employees are recruited, register with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) and implement a workplace health and safety prevention program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (canada.ca/cra-business-registration); Revenu Québec — Entreprise Revenu Québec portal for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), source deductions, and provincial registrations (revenuquebec.ca). The Quebec enterprise number is issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec Limited Partnership (société en commandite), no separate income-tax entity number is issued because income tax is assessed on partners. The statutory tax identification consists of the CRA Business Number (BN) and the Revenu Québec file/QST number. Procedure: (1) register the extra-provincial limited partnership or the non-resident general partner with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Quebec establishment number; (2) register the partnership for a CRA Business Number through Business Registration Online, selecting the GST/HST account and, if applicable, payroll account; (3) within the same CRA registration flow, elect to register with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial source-deduction accounts; (4) appoint a representative with a Canadian nexus for service of notices and returns; (5) retain the CRA BN and RQ file number as the VAT/TIN identifiers for GST/HST and QST purposes respectively. Non-resident partners may also need to provide Form RC519 or equivalent information to document their Canadian contact; Stripe and Paddle onboarding will require the BN and QST numbers for Quebec-based sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box entity-classification regime. A limited partnership is statutorily transparent for income tax; each partner includes its share of income/loss. No entity-level election can make the partnership a corporation. Available elections are limited to ancillary timing/allocation matters, such as partnership fiscal-period elections under Income Tax Act subsection 96(3), and the partner-level choice to treat a foreign partnership as transparent or opaque under the foreign-entity classification rules when cross-border hybrid elements are present. Hybrid mismatch consequences are addressed through the OECD MLI and the Canadian hybrid mismatch rules (Part VI.1 and related provisions); there is no elective regime to alter the default pass-through classification for Canadian income tax purposes. For GST/HST and QST, the partnership itself is a registerable person and may not elect to be disregarded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% administered by the Canada Revenue Agency, plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.5% administered by Revenu Québec; Quebec does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST and QST registration threshold: C$30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for a person carrying on commercial activity in Canada or Quebec. However, a non-resident digital supplier making supplies of software or low-code website-builder services to Canadian or Quebec recipients is required to register for GST/HST and QST without relying on the small-supplier threshold once the C$30,000 threshold in Canadian-source digital revenue is exceeded or where the supply is made in the ordinary course of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. Electronic invoicing is voluntary; tax authorities accept invoices in PDF, XML, and structured e-commerce formats. Compliance is enforced through periodic GST/HST/QST return filing, electronic remittance via CRA My Business Account or Revenu Québec Entreprise portal, and audit production of records. CRA and Revenu Québec support API-based file transfer and machine-readable transaction logs; a foreign LP must retain point-of-sale, billing, and payment records in a format that can be queried on audit. No unique fiscal clearance code or invoice authorization is required before issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported services and digital property applies under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act for GST/HST, and under corresponding provisions of the Quebec Sales Tax Act for QST, when the supply is made to a non-resident person, the service or digital template is not for consumption, use, or enjoyment in Canada or Quebec, and the supplier has documentary evidence of export performance. A no-code website builder selling visual templates and hosting access to a non-resident customer qualifies as an exported intangible supply if delivered electronically outside Canada, the recipient is a non-resident, payment is received from abroad in foreign currency, and there is no Canadian-resident end-user or on-premise performance in Canada. Zero-rating is denied where the recipient is a Canadian resident, the supply is for use partly in Canada, or the supplier has a permanent establishment through which the service is supplied into Canada. If the LP directly supplies to a Quebec consumer, GST and QST at standard rates apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for tangible media or equipment crossing the border; not required for pure cloud-delivered software)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (for physical shipments; not applicable to digital low-code website-builder delivery)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank advice confirming foreign-currency payment and FX conversion within 180 days
Executed SaaS, software license, or digital-template supply agreement identifying the non-resident recipient and describing the place of consumption
Delivery and usage logs showing remote access, geolocation, IP addresses, and timestamps demonstrating consumption outside Canada
Non-resident status certificate, tax-residence certificate, or validated recipient self-declaration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating if export documentation is incomplete, submissions are inconsistent with Stripe or Paddle settlement records, or the transaction shows Canadian end-users. Reassessment and clawback periods are generally six years from the notice of assessment, with no limitation period for misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud. Penalties under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act include late-filing penalties, failure-to-register penalties of up to C$250, and false-statement penalties of 25% of the net tax understated; gross-negligence penalties can be higher and interest compounds daily. Revenu Québec imposes analogous penalties, can freeze refunds, revoke QST registration, and may require a deposit or security for non-resident vendors. Criminal prosecution and director/officer liability may apply for fraudulent export zero-rating claims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (declaration annuelle) confirming partnership identity, registered office, general and limited partners, and business activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the LP registration date, every year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing doubles the fee to approximately USD 54; two consecutive years of non-filing trigger REQ strike-off (radiation) after formal notice; reinstatement requires payment of arrears and filing of current data.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Form T5013) and T5013 Summary, with T5013 slips issued to each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period (e.g., by May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ITA s. 162(4) penalty: CAD 40 per day of default, minimum CAD 500, maximum CAD 2,500; unreported Canadian-source income allocations remain taxable to partners and may trigger Part XIII withholding reassessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Releve 15 (RL-15) information slips and annual RL-15 summary for each Quebec-resident partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which the partnership fiscal period ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under s. 23.0.1 of the Tax Administration Act (Quebec): 5% of unreported amounts plus 0.5% per month up to 12 months; repeated failures may trigger additional penalties and public disclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return (Form GST34) and any balance due, when the LP is a GST/HST registrant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual GST/HST filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; interest at the prescribed rate applies to both arrears and penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ/QST) annual return and remittance, when the LP is a QST registrant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual QST filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same penalty grid as GST/HST (5% plus 1% per month, maximum 12 months) plus arrears interest under the Tax Administration Act (Quebec).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit for a Quebec limited partnership carrying on a low-risk software business. An audit is compulsory if: (a) the LP or its general partner is a reporting issuer under Quebec securities law or NI 51-102; (b) the LP is an investment plan within ITA s. 149.1(1)(d.1) or s. 197; (c) the partnership agreement or a lender covenant requires an audit (typical where limited partners exceed 100 or non-resident capital is material); or (d) the general partner itself is subject to a statutory audit. Absent these triggers, a review engagement (CPA Canada Handbook Section 8200) or notice-to-reader compilation is sufficient.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) applies only to publicly accountable enterprises; private software-development LPs apply Canadian ASPE (Part II). US-GAAP may be used for internal US-partner reporting but not as the primary statutory basis. Books must be retained for 6 years under ITA s. 230(4) and Quebec tax law; this model uses a 7-year safe-harbor retention period covering extended reassessment windows.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each annual REQ declaration re-discloses the name and address of every general and limited partner. Any change in partners or partnership agreement must be filed with REQ as an amending declaration within 30 days of the change. The LP must maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control (direct or indirect 25%+ economic interest); although Bill 78's mandatory beneficial-ownership register applies to legal persons rather than LPs, prudent practice is to verify and update the UBO register annually and deliver it to REQ within 30 days on request. Non-resident partners' ownership data must also support T5013 allocations and any Part XIII withholding positions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners per Civil Code of Quebec art. 2241, kept at the Quebec establishment
Minute Book of General Partner resolutions and partner consents
Register of Beneficial Ownership / Individuals with Significant Control (recommended at the 25% threshold)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 220 - 650 (CAD 300 - 900) for a standard Quebec registered-office and registered-agent arrangement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,800 - 13,000 for a full audit when contractually or legally triggered; 2,200 - 5,100 for a review engagement; 900 - 1,900 for a notice-to-reader compilation

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined corporate rate for corporate partners (15% federal general + 11.5% Quebec general); the Canadian Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and is not assessed at the entity level. Non-resident individual partners are taxed at federal/provincial progressive personal rates on their allocable share.
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory 'tax holiday' applies; effective reductions include the Small Business Deduction (federal 9% + Quebec reduced 3.2% on the first C$500,000 of eligible active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner, reducing combined rates to approx. 12.2%), the SR&ED federal investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs on qualifying R&D expenditures within prescribed CRA limits, 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs), the Quebec SR&ED/R&D tax credit (up to 30% on eligible salaries and qualifiable expenditures for qualifying SMEs), and the Quebec Patent Box deduction (eligible income from commercialized patents/technology know-how may be reduced by the prescribed deduction quantum). Software-as-a-service subscription revenue is not eligible for a patent-royalty statutory holiday unless protected patents are exploited.
